title: Call for proposals for action grants to support transnational projects in the fields of e-Justice, victims’ rights and procedural rights
description: Expected Outcome: The call for proposals aims to facilitate effective and non-discriminatory access to justice for all, and effective redress, including by electronic means (e-Justice), by promoting efficient civil, and criminal procedures, and by promoting and supporting the rights of all victims of crime as well as the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. This biennial call for proposals, under the Access to justice specific objective, covers two priorities: E-justice priority Victims’ rights and procedural rights priority This topic is covering the Victims' rights and procedural rights priority of the call for proposals for EU action grants to support transnational projects in the fields of e-Justice, victims’ rights and procedural rights under the Justice Programme (JUST) . For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the call document

title: European Joint Programme on agricultural soil management
description: The EJP SOIL "Access to Infrastructure" call is targeting researchers and technical staff from institutions outside the EJP SOIL consortium who intend to improve research and enhance collaboration with EU soil laboratories and LTEs. The call will provide financial support to researchers outside of the EJP SOIL consortium and fund physical visits (travel and accommodation costs) to European Long-term experimental sites (LTEs) and/or laboratories (LABs). An overview over EU LTEs/LABs that might be of interest for applicants can be found in the EJP SOIL database: https://ejpsoil.eu/long-term-field-experiments-laboratories . In the case of soil sampling or analyses in addition to the physical visit of a non-EJP SOIL visitor at facilities that are linked to the EJP SOIL, these costs will be covered by the EJP SOIL host institution from their EJP SOIL budget (WP7).
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Submission preparation The "Access to Infrastructure" call of the European Joint Programme EJP SOIL is presented on the EJP SOIL webpage ( https://ejpsoil.eu/long-term-field-experiments-laboratories ). The invitation to submit applications ( https://ejpsoil.eu/long-term-field-experiments-laboratories/invitation ), as well as the necessary documents, i.e., application templates, consent form, financial consent form, and reporting form (after the visit/project) are posted on the webpage ( https://ejpsoil.eu/visiting-scientists-support ) at least 15 days prior to the launch of the call. The call will be open for 2 months with a deadline on 31.05.2023. In addition to the application form, applicants will need to submit a CV, a consent form signed by the applicant and a financial consent form signed by the applicant’s institution’s financial officer. In the financial consent form, the applicant should add information on the staff type (e.g., researcher, PhD student, technician), travel and subsistence costs. Submission The filled in and signed application form, the CV, the applicant´s consent form, and the financial consent form shall be sent by mail to katharina.meurer@slu.se no later than 31.05.2023. Evaluation Applications will be evaluated by an Evaluation Committee consisting of researchers from institutions linked to EJP SOIL. The Committee will evaluate the applications according to: (i) the scientific value of the visit/project; (ii) the compatibility of the proposed activity with the EJP SOIL aims and scope; and, (iii) the relevance of the proposed activity to EJP SOIL´s Expected Impacts. Individual applicants will be informed within 2 weeks of the deadline on the result of their application. A limited number of grants will be reserved for applicants from non-European countries. The acceptance of the application depends on the number and success rate of applicants received from European countries. Priority is given to European applications.
furtherInformation:
The "Access to Infrastructure" call of the European Joint Programme “EJP SOIL - Towards climate-smart sustainable management of agricultural soils” aims at facilitating access of non-EJP SOIL researchers to European Long-term field experimental sites (LTEs) and/or Soil Laboratories (LABs) by financially supporting them. The activities of the granted applications have to be related to the scope of the EJP SOIL. This is considered an important opportunity to obtain additional analyses, foster harmonization of methods and databases, and exchange expertise with researchers and technicians at the EU level.

The EJP SOIL call for access to infrastructure is launched two times per year (April and September). The calls are in line with the EJP SOIL Impact pathway EI 3 “Strengthening scientific capacities and cooperation across Europe including training of young soil scientists”.  The maximum amount of funding that can be asked for per applicant is 5000 € to cover physical visits to facilities, such as LTEs and LABs.

title: European City Facility
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The EUCF is open to all municipalities/local authorities, their groupings, and local public entities aggregating municipalities/local authorities from the 27 EU Member States, Iceland and Ukraine. Applicants are required to have a climate and/or energy plan. This includes SECAPs (Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans), developed within the Covenant of Mayors initiative, or other climate and/or energy plans with mitigation targets. Moreover, applicants have to demonstrate political commitment to the development of the Investment Concept through a letter of support, signed by the Mayor or other relevant political representative. The applicant must commit to the EUCF monitoring period of two years. The grant cannot directly finance the actual investments, but it covers costs to mobilise resources and access services to develop an investment concept. Applications are evaluated based on 4 evaluation criteria: Ambition of the proposed investment concept Governance structure for the development of the investment concept Stakeholders engagement strategy Coherence and plausibility The overall application process consists of an (1) eligibility check and in (2) filling in an application form. Once successfully passing this eligibility check, performed by the applicants themselves directly on the EUCF website, the applicant will be directed to the online portal that includes the application form to be filled in and submitted. The application form is accessible online via the EUCF website during the whole application period. The EUCF calls are organised in parallel for three geographic regions including all eligible countries (EU 27 Member States, Iceland and Ukraine): Central and Eastern Europen region: Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Ukraine. Nordic countries & Western European region: Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden. Southern European region: Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Malta, Portugal, Spain.
furtherInformation:
The European City Facility (EUCF) aims to support municipalities and local authorities in developing Investment Concepts related to the implementation of actions identified in their climate and energy action plans. The ultimate objective of the EUCF is to build a substantial pipeline of sustainable energy investment projects across municipalities in Europe.

The EUCF provides you support for the development of an Investment Concept with a fixed grant of 60 000 EUR per beneficiary.

The EUCF finances activities, such as (technical) feasibility studies, market analyses, stakeholder analyses, legal, economic and financial analyses, risk analyses, etc., that are required to develop the investment concept. These activities can be delivered by in-house staff or subcontracted external experts.

All information an application form available in www.eucityfacility.eu.

title: Joint Cluster Initiatives (EUROCLUSTERS) for Europe’s recovery
description: This call targets innovative SMEs developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams , contributing to more sustainable and resilient agri-food ecosystems through the development of new processes, services and products. This Innovation Call includes financial support for projects especially focusing on the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients for food and non-food applications, products, business processes, and technologies (including digital) that maximise the valorisation of agri-food biomass and side-streams . These projects should have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6. 1.The Innovation Open Call targets: SMEs in the agri-food production and/or processing sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise their own biomass/by-products/side-streams for the agri-food sector; SMEs offering solutions and/or technology for the valorisation of biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector (development and application of new technologies or processes). 2.The applicant’s project must lead to the implementation of either a new process, a new product, or a new service or a combination of them . 3.Proposals can be submitted either by a single SME or by an SMEs consortium with up to three (3) SMEs . 4.Applicants can be SMEs registered at EU Member States and countries associated to the Single Market Programme. 5. Projects must have a minimum Technology Readiness Level ( TRL ) of at least 6. 6.For Single SME projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (1 SME) is €60.000 . 7.For collaborative projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (2-3 SMEs) is €90.000 . 8.Innovation grants must be matched by at least 15% private financial contribution (debt or own financial resources), with proof required. AMENDMENT 16 JULY 2026 Following aspects of the call text have been updated and clarified: Thematic priorities - scope of the call and valorisation pathways Call definitions: biosolutions added, TRL requirements clarified Documents required: no stamp needed, only signature Eligibility criteria Evaluation procedure, criteria and scoring: 2 stage evaluation process in Cut-off 2, pre-selection (knock-out stage) added. Timing of the evaluation procedure cut-off 2 prolonged Re-submission of proposals: to be done in new application form Period to file complaints SPOC contact details Pay attention that there is an adapted application form for cut-off 2!
